persona.who: 25, Tamil-Singaporean analyst at a bank, first in family to go to university, got promoted early, feels she doesn't belong in the room.
persona.note: got promoted ahead of people with MBAs. in every meeting I think they're going to find out I'm just the girl from the HDB whose dad drove a taxi. I over prepare for everything and still feel sick before presenting

understanding.core_struggle: She was promoted over people, and now feels she will be exposed as a fraud; she overprepares and still feels sick before presenting.
understanding.mirror: You prepare more than anyone, and still your stomach turns before you speak.
understanding.insight: It isn't the MBA that keeps you up. It's the voice that says your father's taxi is your ceiling, and that you are only in the room until they find out.

queries.hook: The fear that your rise is a mistake and everyone will see you do not belong, even when you have earned the place. I feel like an imposter.
queries.diagnose: When the mind believes it is not enough, every success is read as luck; self-blame grows from measuring your worth against a picture you were never meant to fit.
queries.steady: The one who keeps pushing themselves down becomes their own enemy; lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down.
queries.act: Speak the true thing about your work to yourself before you enter the room, and let your preparation be enough without demanding it be perfect.
queries.story: A young woman who rose above her beginnings, stood before a room that doubted her, and found her own footing when the doubt was loudest.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
verse.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
verse.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
verse.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verse.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
verse.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

prasang.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands in his chariot between two armies and sees his own family. He does not raise his bow. His limbs shake, his mouth goes dry, his body trembles. The Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero. Even the strongest people freeze. The teaching begins there.
verse.for_you: That sick feeling before you present is not a sign you are failing. It is a body that cares. Let it be there while you speak, and let the shaking be part of what carries you through the room.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira in the forest. She tells him never to look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity. Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you. Effort still matters. Fate rewards no one who waits.
verse.for_you: Your overpreparing is a form of waiting. It asks the future to prove you are good enough. Today, do one thing for its own sake, not to prove anything. Let the work stand on its own and see what it gives back.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after he has lost his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt, and not to settle for too little. Set your mind on what is truly good, and stop fearing. Pull yourself together.
verse.for_you: You are not your father's taxi. You are not a mistake waiting to be found out. Set your mind on what is truly good in the room, and let that be enough to pull you through the day.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
verse.line: Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
verse.translation: For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Staying steady under insult is not accepting mistreatment; you can stay calm and still speak up.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna is with Arjuna on the battlefield, telling him that the self-mastered person remains steady when praise and insult come. The one who has conquered themselves stays centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour. Their higher self does not shake, because they are no longer at war with themselves. This steadiness is not a mask. It is the result of choosing to be your own friend rather than your own worst enemy.
verse.for_you: When you stand to present, feel the room and the fear. You do not need to prove yourself to them, or to your father's taxi. You only need to be your own friend right now.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that his right is only to the work itself, never to its fruits. Do not let the outcome be the reason you act, and do not let the fear of the outcome stop you from acting. The work is yours to do fully. The results are not yours to hold, so you can act without being chained to what comes next.
verse.for_you: You are spending four hours a day overthinking your next presentation. Do your part with full attention, and then step away from the outcome. Your worth is not decided by how the room receives your words.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a free person does the work in front of them, speaks gently, and reads the hearts of others. They do not grieve over what is lost, nor do they crave what they do not have. They move through the world unhurried and calm inside, treating everyone as family. This is how one stays afloat in the world without sinking.
verse.for_you: In your next meeting, do the work that is in front of you. Speak gently, even when you feel the old doubt rising. Read the room for what it is, not for what you fear it might become. Let your inside stay calm while your outside does the job.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

prasang.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.for_you: You have the skills and the strength already. You do not need to out-prepare the others to prove you belong in that room. Step into the leap.

weeks.title: The voice that says you don't belong

script: You are sitting in the meeting room and you feel that familiar wave of heat. The promotion is real, but the voice in your head is louder. It tells you that your father's taxi is your ceiling and you are only in the room until they find out.

On the field, Arjuna stands in his chariot between two armies. He looks at the faces of his own kin and teachers. They are on the other side. He does not raise his bow. His limbs shake and his mouth goes dry. And Arjuna said:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति, वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते. गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते, न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः.
In plain words: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.

The Gita opens with a breakdown, not a hero. Even the strongest people freeze. Your body is doing exactly what a brave person's body does when the stakes are high. It is not a sign of weakness. It is a body that cares deeply about what is at stake.
Before you present, let that sick feeling be there. Let the shaking be part of what carries you through the room. You do not need to silence the fear to do your best work.
Your body is not failing you. It is feeling the weight of what you have built.

depth.life: You sit at your desk and run through the presentation in your head for the tenth time. Your hands are cold, and you feel the familiar nausea rising before you even open the door. You are ready, but your body does not believe it.
depth.points: Arjuna was the greatest warrior on the field, and his body betrayed him. The Gita does not begin with a hero. It begins with a man who knows his duty and is terrified. The breakdown is not a sign of weakness. It is the raw material of the teaching.
depth.practice: Before you start your next meeting, notice the sensation in your hands. Let your fingers rest on the table and feel the temperature of the air on your skin. Do this for one minute.
depth.question: What would change if you let the shaking be part of your presence?
